topic_brief.title: No-till vs conventional tillage effects on crop yield
topic_brief.research_question: Does no-till management affect crop yield compared to conventional tillage, and how does this vary by crop type and climate?
topic_brief.population_description: Crop plants grown in field experiments comparing tillage systems
topic_brief.intervention_description: No-till or zero-till management (seeds planted directly into undisturbed soil)
topic_brief.comparator_description: Conventional tillage (moldboard plow, disk, chisel, or other inversion/intensive tillage)
topic_brief.outcome_description: Crop grain yield per unit area
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is NO-TILL (less disturbance), Control is CONVENTIONAL TILLAGE (more disturbance)
Reduced tillage is NOT no-till - if both exist, compare no-till vs conventional
Some papers have 3+ tillage levels - extract the no-till vs most intensive tillage comparison
Strip-till is intermediate - do not include as no-till unless paper explicitly calls it no-till
Long-term trials may show different effects in early vs late years - extract each year separately
topic_brief.benchmark_notes: Overall -5.7%; Wheat -2.6%; Maize -7.6%; Rice -7.5%; Soybean +0.3%; Oilseed rape -9.0%

rows.control_description: Conventional tillage with cover crops, no N fertilization (CTN0)

rows.title: Long-term analysis of soil water conservation and crop yield under different tillage systems in Mediterranean rainfed conditions
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage (NT), direct seeding without soil disturbance
rows.control_description: Subsoiler 50 cm depth (Sub-50), most intensive tillage at this site
rows.notes: Tillage effect on yield not significant at El Canós (P>0.05). SD values are temporal (across 8 years of data), not within-year spatial variability. Mean is averaged over all years and replicates (4 blocks). Only 3 tillage systems at this site: NT, MT, Sub-50. Sub-50 is the only intensive tillage system available. No LSD significance letters shown for yield, confirming NS result.

moderators.mod_region: El Canós, Ebro Valley, NE Spain
moderators.mod_residue_management: removed (straw cut and removed, stubble left 20-25 cm)

rows.title: Long-term analysis of soil water conservation and crop yield under different tillage systems in Mediterranean rainfed conditions
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage (NT), direct seeding without soil disturbance
rows.control_description: Mouldboard plough (Mb), 30-35 cm depth + 1-2 cultivator passes at 15 cm
rows.notes: Significant tillage effect on yield (P<0.0001). NT ranked 'a', Mb ranked 'c' by LSD(0.05). SD values are temporal (across 19 years), not within-year spatial variability. Mean averaged over all years and replicates (4 blocks). Agramunt is the driest site (highest water deficit). Yield ranking: NT > Sub-50 > Ch = Mb. Mb had lowest yields especially in dry years (<2000 kg/ha). TIL*YEAR interaction significant (P<0.0001).

moderators.mod_residue_management: retained (straw chopped and spread by combine)

rows.title: Long-term analysis of soil water conservation and crop yield under different tillage systems in Mediterranean rainfed conditions
rows.treatment_description: No-tillage (NT), direct seeding without soil disturbance
rows.control_description: Subsoiler 50 cm depth (Sub-50), most intensive tillage at this site
rows.notes: Significant tillage effect on yield (P<0.0001). NT ranked 'a', Sub-50 ranked 'c' by LSD(0.05). SD values are temporal (across 19 years), not within-year spatial variability. Mean averaged over all years and replicates (3 blocks). Selvanera is the wettest site (lowest water deficit). Yield ranking: NT(a) >= MT(ab) >= Sub-25(bc) >= Sub-50(c). Differences mainly in less-productive years. TIL*YEAR interaction significant (P<0.0001). Canola has ~1800 kg/ha lower intercept than cereals.
